stories.headline: Todd asks if his golf handicap transfers to the standings
stories.dek: Todd is 7-15 and Seth is 8-14, with a year off waiting for whoever finishes last.
body: Todd is 2-9 against the median. At his meat stand, he can put his thumb on the scale. In fantasy, he puts his thumb on the scale and ESPN asks if he'd like to make Jordyn Tyson his captain. Tyson gave him 2.0 last week. The thumb is requesting a trade.

Todd went from 176.9 in Week 10 to 100.0 in Week 11. That's the golf swing he keeps telling everybody felt great until he looked up. Meanwhile Seth has lost three straight in the standings and scored 91.7 last week. Brock Bowers contributed 0.0. You could put that number on a name tag and have it stand behind the counter pretending to manage the store.

Todd gets Scott and then Bryan. Scott leads the league and Bryan is second, which makes this a lovely time for Todd to discover that a family discount does not apply to a loss. Seth gets Chad and then Burnie. Beating Chad would drag a 9-13 team closer to the mess. Chad is a pastor, so somebody should tell him that visiting the basement is technically a charitable act and that he can do it after the season.

Todd can erase the gap by outwinning Seth in the head-to-head and median games that are left. Seth can keep Todd underneath him by matching him from here. This is the first time all year Todd has had a compelling reason to look at Seth's lineup. Imagine checking another man's flex with the exact intensity of somebody in a parking lot trying to remember whether that's his car getting towed.

stories.headline: Doug buys the Packers defense and asks if it comes with a warranty
stories.dek: Doug spent $107 on the Packers defense and $52 on Austin Ekeler in Wednesday's waiver run.
body: Doug paid $107 to exchange the Patriots defense for the Packers defense. At his produce stand you usually get to squeeze something before you pay that much for it. On waivers you get a tiny helmet and the opportunity to squeeze your phone on Sunday until the battery comes out.

He also paid $52 for Austin Ekeler, bringing the morning's bill to $159. The defense is the item he came into the store for. Ekeler is what he grabbed while waiting for the cashier to find somebody authorized to sell him a defense. Imagine the cashier asking whether Doug found everything he needed and Doug pointing very confidently at a receipt that contains absolutely no points.

Burnie paid $75 apiece for Deshaun Watson and Bam Knight. There's a lovely symmetry to that. The receipt looks like the league held a silent auction and Burnie wrote the same number on every clipboard he passed on the way to the bathroom. The real danger is that he now has two new players to stare at while trying to remember which one inspired him to open the app.

Seth spent $50 to swap Brandon Aiyuk for Jack Bech. Thatcher spent $36 to turn Kalif Raymond into the Giants defense, a week after claiming Raymond for $0. That is a perfectly respectable way to run a pawn shop if you remember to charge the guy on the other side of the counter. Thatcher apparently prefers to hand the man his own merchandise back, tuck cash into his pocket and remind him to tell Randy he got lucky.

stories.headline: Chad finds a quarterback in the change tray
stories.dek: Chad's $8 claim on C.J. Stroud has returned 148.7 points across five starts.
body: Chad paid $8 for C.J. Stroud and has collected 148.7 points in five starts. That's the kind of purchase you make when the self-checkout rings up a television as an onion and you suddenly get very interested in putting the receipt in your pocket and walking at a normal speed. Chad oversees church building projects. If he gets the same return on lumber, somebody should start checking the steeple for a second steeple.

Dwayne paid $175 for Jordan Love and got 125.7 in five starts. He also paid nothing for Braelon Allen and got 93.8 in six starts. The two receipts look like Dwayne negotiated a terrific deal on a refrigerator and then paid full retail for the cardboard box. He's hung enough drywall to know how this works. When the customer wants to know why the estimate doubled, point at the ceiling and start explaining something about studs until he goes back inside.

Then there's Todd, who paid $451 for Ollie Gordon II and got 92.6 points in seven starts. Devaughn Vele cost Todd nothing and has given him 65.9 in six. Picture a man at a carnival clutching a stuffed bear he just spent his wallet winning. That's Todd. The man running the booth is trying to explain that the smaller bear came free with admission. Todd would like everybody to stop looking at the smaller bear. He would also like the guy running the booth to put the basketball back in his hands because he's finally figured out the angle.

stories.headline: Brandon takes the playoff seat and leaves Burnie the Wi-Fi password
stories.dek: Brandon grabbed sixth with 141.5 points while Burnie fell to seventh with a league-low 81.9.
body: Brandon and Burnie share an Airbnb, so both understand what happens when somebody else books the room. They're both 11-11, but Brandon's in sixth and Burnie's out on the porch typing the door code slower.

Brandon scored 141.5. At that point the rental app should have sent Burnie a photo of his brother holding the keys with the caption, Your host is nearby. Your host has also declined your request for a late checkout. He says you had all Sunday. Burnie lost to Doug, who scored 116.4. The median was 113.0, so Burnie managed to get turned away at two separate doors. You have to admire the efficiency. Most people would have wasted an afternoon driving between properties to get rejected that thoroughly.

Burnie DJs weddings. He knows exactly what to do when the dance floor clears, which is why we're begging him to stop looking at 81.9 and reaching for the fog machine. There is no remix where Dobbins comes in on the second verse. That is the entire song. Dak Prescott put up 43.9 for Brandon. Burnie started J.K. Dobbins for 0.0 and finished with 81.9. The checkout instructions are to strip the bed, take out the trash and please stop trying the code.

Imagine the review Burnie could leave for the playoff spot. The listing said it slept six, but the host occupied the last bed and made me stand outside holding a pillow. Lovely property. Would have preferred to stay. One star, because the app won't let me give it what Dobbins gave me.

stories.headline: Roger puts DK Metcalf in the tip jar
stories.dek: Jonah Coleman and CeeDee Lamb carried Roger to a league-high 144.4, with 1.2 from DK Metcalf.
body: Roger rang up 144.4, the week's top score, and DK Metcalf tossed 1.2 into the tip jar like he was apologizing for paying with a large bill.

Roger actually operates a pretzel stand, which makes him uniquely qualified to look at this lineup and instantly know who needs to stop touching the dough. Coleman and Lamb can take a break whenever they like. DK can take a break as soon as somebody notices he came back from the first one. The scoreboard says the rest of the league had a chance. Brandon got to 141.5, close enough to smell the pretzels and discover Roger had just pulled the little metal gate down. Imagine getting 43.9 from Dak Prescott and still having to eat dinner at the mall fountain.

Roger's team is 14-8. The tip screen would like to know whether you want to leave 15 percent, 20 percent or whatever amount will make DK stop making eye contact. There is a custom button. It's just a picture of Roger reaching past you and pressing it himself. Jonah Coleman put up 36.9 and CeeDee Lamb added 31.2. At Roger's pretzel stand, that gets you two employees doing the whole lunch rush while DK stands at the register turning the screen around and asking if you'd like to tip.

Put the receipt on the fridge, Roger. Circle Coleman's number. Circle Lamb's. Fold the bottom up over DK's line like it's the part that tells your spouse what the pretzels actually cost. If anybody asks what he did, tell them he had the little hat on and let them draw their own conclusions.

stories.headline: Thatcher beats first place and is furious to learn about it
stories.dek: Thatcher beat league leader Scott 134.3 to 128.1 and moved into fourth.
body: Thatcher beat first-place Scott by 6.2 points. Please give him some privacy while he figures out whose lucky break this was and how it was meant to ruin his week.

Scott had 128.1 and still won his median game. That's the kind of loss where you get home and find out the valet still gave you the good parking spot. Scott remains first. Thatcher will presumably list that as evidence that beating him accomplished something suspiciously small. Thatcher drives a truck for a lumber company. Imagine him backing up to the standings with a load marked GOOD NEWS and asking the dock guy to check the address again. Surely this goes to Randy. Can you look under Randy? Can you call Randy and ask if he's expecting anything?

Randy is fifth, directly behind Thatcher. This is a terrible place for Randy to stand if he wants to be blamed for fewer things. Thatcher can now turn around and deliver an entire opening statement without moving his feet. The exhibit marked 134.3 will be entered as evidence against his own happiness. Chuba Hubbard scored 28.0 and Travis Kelce added 25.4. Even Michael Mayer's 1.4 couldn't save Thatcher from fourth place. Imagine spending all week boarding up the windows and having good news come down the chimney.

At 12-10, Thatcher has a playoff spot to defend. Somebody should tell him it's a particularly grim assignment. He'll have to trudge back to his phone and look at the same standings the rest of us look at for fun. The man finally has a cushion and he's checking it for termites.

stories.headline: Todd put up 100 and left Dwayne a step stool
stories.dek: Todd leads 100.0 to 75.5, but Dwayne has three Monday starters left and a 120.5 projection.
body: Todd put up 100.0 and left Dwayne the kind of obstacle a drywall guy steps over while carrying drywall. Dwayne has 75.5 with Ja'Marr Chase, Chig Okonkwo and Antonio Williams still to go. The app projects 120.5. Todd can spend Monday night defending his lead by holding his phone very still, the same technique you use when a wasp lands on your french fry.

Todd likes to propose a wager whenever he plays Dwayne. The loser has to kiss the winner's bare backside. You'd think a guy who keeps bringing this idea to the meeting would eventually bring a scoreboard that could clear his browser history. Tonight the projection says Todd should put the paperwork down and practice saying he was obviously kidding. He's going to want that sentence to sound spontaneous.

Chase alone is projected for 25.9, more than Todd's entire cushion. If Chase gets there, Okonkwo and Williams can spend the rest of the evening ringing Todd's doorbell and running away. If Chase falls short, Dwayne still has two other starters available to complete the job. Todd has the refresh button, which lets him ask whether the people doing the work have finished yet.

The median could make the evening even ruder. Todd is above it right now and projects below it. Dwayne is below it right now and projects above it. That's an awful lot of furniture for Dwayne to move into the apartment before Todd realizes who's on the lease. Todd, if the score holds, by all means celebrate. Maybe leave the proposed wager out of the group chat until the drywall dries.

stories.headline: The median is checking Bryan's height at the gate
stories.dek: Bryan has Tee Higgins left and projects to finish 1.1 points below the median.
body: Bryan has 97.3, a lead over Randy's 94.0 and one starter left in Tee Higgins. Lovely. Now stand up straight, Bryan. The ride attendant says your projected 114.4 still comes in 1.1 points below the line. You can absolutely keep the head-to-head lead and spend the whole ride watching the other kids go around from the bench beside the world's saddest coin-operated horse.

The median is at 98.7 right now and projects to reach 115.4. This is the amusement park where the height requirement goes up while you're standing under the sign. If Higgins runs a route for twelve yards and Bryan starts celebrating, somebody check whether the kid with the clipboard just put on thicker shoes.

Randy has no starters left, so his contribution to the rest of this matchup is getting out of the way. Bryan can still take the points Randy left sitting there and somehow come home furious at the concept of six other people. He's 8-2 against the median coming in, which gives him just enough experience with this particular ride to be the loudest guy in line when the teenager with the clipboard tells him to step aside.

Higgins is projected for 17.0, which makes him the only employee in this operation who can do anything about the height stick. Bryan will be squinting at every catch like he's checking whether a coupon has expired. Somewhere in the app there should be a button that just tells him to take his shoes off and try again.

stories.headline: Seth's comeback plan has a small Bengals infestation
stories.dek: Seth trails Roger by 28.7 points, and both lineups still have starters in Monday’s Cincinnati-Washington game.
body: Seth needs a comeback and has submitted the Bengals defense as part of his application. Roger, who already leads 111.9 to 83.2, still has Joe Burrow and Chase Brown. Imagine breaking into a vending machine and finding Roger inside eating the chips. That's roughly the amount of Cincinnati Seth has to work around before anybody checks whether his comeback paperwork is even in the right folder.

Seth also has Stefon Diggs, so he's rooting for Washington to throw to Diggs and for Cincinnati's defense to do something impressive on all the other plays. That's a workable viewing plan if you've got a separate remote for each play and the commissioner lets you rewind any drive that inconveniences you. Roger gets to watch Burrow and Brown. Seth has to watch the game like a parent trying to get two kids to share one desirable chicken nugget.

The projections put Roger at 156.6 and Seth at 101.2. The app has effectively assigned Seth a middle seat and put both armrests in Roger's name. There's room for Monday to surprise everybody, which is precisely the sort of sentence you say to a man in a middle seat while he's discovering that the person in front of him can recline.

Seth has a habit of telling everyone how much more he cares about his other fantasy leagues. Monday is an excellent night to have those tabs open. Every time Burrow puts more points on Roger's side, Seth can click over and remember that this league occupies a very small, unimportant place in his life. He can tell us all about it immediately after checking the score again.

stories.headline: C.J. Stroud did the group project and Chad still might fail
stories.dek: Stroud put up 27.5, but the 9-11 Fishsticks are still projected to lose to the 9-11 Bike slashers.
body: C.J. Stroud handed Chad 27.5 points and an early lead. The projection still has the Fishsticks losing 115.4 to 103.1. Imagine doing the whole group project yourself and watching Chad eat the poster board on presentation day.

Jonathan Taylor has 6.7 points so far for Brandon. That's a lovely little contribution if you're buying a sandwich and the cashier asks whether you'd like to round up. David Montgomery put up 17.4. Brandon, if Dak and Pickens rescue this thing, Montgomery gets to sit in the front on the drive home. Taylor can hold the leftovers upright on his lap.

Chad's lineup still has Germie Bernard, projected for 3.2. That's the amount of points you find between the couch cushions when you go looking for the remote. Unfortunately, the Fishsticks need the remote. The projection has them 14.1 below the median, and the only button Chad can reach from here is the one that makes the same score reload.

Chad's Wi-Fi made the Phillies buffer at the draft. If his matchup page freezes on the current score Sunday, somebody needs to get over there and unplug the router before he starts taking screenshots for the playoff committee. Brandon, if you do pass him, let him keep the screenshot. He can frame it next to the participation ribbon the printer is still buffering.

Both teams are a win behind sixth-place Thatcher. Brandon still has Dak Prescott and George Pickens to play. Chad still has Amon-Ra St. Brown, who should probably bring a second poster board and keep it somewhere Chad can't reach.

stories.headline: Doug would like to apply his golf handicap to the median
stories.dek: The Cow Tippers are projected to beat Burnie and still finish 0.4 points below the median.
body: Doug is 8-12 and projected to beat Burnie, which is lovely until you see his 116.8 sitting just under the 117.2 median. This is exactly when Doug would set down his golf bag and explain for twenty minutes why the computer owes him strokes.

Burnie still has Bo Nix and J.K. Dobbins in the same late-afternoon Denver game. Doug will have to watch them take turns touching his lead like kids who have been explicitly told to keep their hands off the cake. Then he'll get to the night game and discover that the cake is also competing against five other cakes for a playoff-relevant win.

The Cow Tippers have a 3-7 head-to-head record and a 5-5 median record. Doug has basically been getting more Christmas cards from strangers than from the people he actually knows. Now the app thinks he'll beat the guy he's playing and lose to the people minding their own business. Doug, this is why everyone asks who's coming before they agree to golf with you.

Burnie enters at 11-9. If his team gets both losses the projection suggests, somebody at his next wedding should request a moment of silence for the Ballers' weekend. Give it the full treatment. Dim the lights, have everyone put their phones away, then announce that Doug has asked for extra strokes on the dance floor.

Brock Purdy, Justin Jefferson and George Kittle all play Sunday night. Doug gets to spend the evening refreshing three players for four tenths of a point. Burnie DJs weddings, so if that lead evaporates, at least somebody here knows how to fade out a song while Doug is still dancing.

stories.headline: Bryan puts Randy's lead under the pretzel warmer
stories.dek: Randy leads 18.6 to 5.7 so far, but Bryan is projected to win and enters the week one game ahead in the standings.
body: Randy has 18.6 points on the board to Bryan's 5.7, and the forecast still favors Bryan, 118.8 to 113.2. Bryan owns Auntie Anne's franchises, so he knows how to display an unappetizing number until somebody pays full price for it.

Nico Collins already supplied 15.3 of Randy's points. Tank Dell supplied all 5.7 of Bryan's. If these scores were samples at the mall, Randy would hand you a pretzel and Bryan would hand you the toothpick it came on. Then Bryan would point to the projection and ask how many toothpicks you'd like to order for your next corporate event.

Bryan enters at 13-7 and Randy at 12-8. Bryan is also 8-2 against the median, which explains why he can look so pleased with himself while sporting a 5-5 head-to-head record. You can beat him in the matchup and he'll still find a way to validate his parking. Imagine being Randy and having to beat a guy who brought a second receipt.

Randy still has Rashee Rice alongside Mahomes. Every Mahomes touchdown to Rice would give Bryan the pleasant experience of paying for the same pretzel twice. Bryan is currently projected above the median and Randy below, so there's room for the scoreboard to make both of them miserable in different ways. If the app asks Bryan to tip at checkout, we'd like to watch him choose a percentage.
Patrick Mahomes still has to play for Randy. If he cooks, Bryan can spend Sunday twisting the standings into a shape he likes better. At least he'll already have the uniform.

stories.headline: Roger traded Jaylen Warren and kept the packing peanuts
stories.dek: Randy has banked 140.9 starting points from Warren since the September swap, while Roger has gotten 12.7 from Jadarian Price.
body: Roger traded Jaylen Warren to Randy for Jadarian Price in September, which is a perfectly sensible move if your fantasy app opens to the Donate tab. Warren has scored 140.9 points in seven starts for Randy. Price has scored 12.7 in two starts for Roger. You could subtract the difference, or you could turn your calculator upside down and see if it spells HELP.

The sneaky part is that Price had scored 12.8 in Randy's lineup before the swap. Roger has gotten within a tenth of recreating the exact amount of Jadarian Price that Randy was willing to part with. It's like buying somebody's treadmill and finding out the previous owner also used it to hang exactly two shirts.

Warren, meanwhile, had put up 20.0 points as a Smoketown starter before the trade. Randy got him home and apparently pulled the little plastic tab out of the battery compartment. Seven starts later the thing is still working. Roger, check the box again. Sometimes the instructions are printed underneath the part you mailed to fourth place.

The most aggravating part for everybody else is that Roger and Randy are both 12-8. Smoketown is third and Randy is fourth. Roger handed the guy directly behind him a running back who has averaged 20.1 points per start since the deal, then had the nerve to stay one line above him in the standings. Imagine getting your lunch stolen and making the thief carry your backpack to class. Randy, you can put it down whenever.

stories.headline: Brandon has eight playoff stamps and one ancient trophy
stories.dek: The Bike slashers sit eighth after eight straight playoff appearances in the available records, still chasing Brandon's first title since 2004.
body: Brandon has made the playoffs eight times in eight seasons on file. He also won the league's inaugural championship in 2004, which means his trophy has been collecting dust long enough to qualify as an archaeological discovery. He's been back to the playoffs every year in the available records, but the trophy shelf hasn't needed an expansion permit. At this point, the league should put a little cardboard cutout of him beside the trophy that says you must be this close to ride. He keeps qualifying and somehow still ends up holding everybody's jackets.

The record book gives Brandon a 110-99 all-time record, including the current season, with eight playoff appearances and a championship from 2004. It's an impressive résumé, even if that trophy is now old enough to have opinions about property taxes. Put the numbers on a banner, but hang it low enough that somebody can use it as a napkin at the trophy dinner.

Last season was his first runner-up finish. Brandon entered as the second seed at 20-8. Randy entered as the fifth seed at 15-13 and took the title. Imagine walking into the final with five more regular-season wins and finding out the only thing they bought you was a better seat for Randy's presentation.

Now the Bike slashers are eighth at 9-11, with four weeks left and six playoff spots. For once Brandon is making the part before the playoffs suspenseful. The league could save itself some time and have him hand out his own invitations. Dear everyone, please join me for my annual postseason appearance. Gifts are discouraged, unless you've found a replacement trophy case for the one I bought in 2004. Randy, you already know where to park.

stories.headline: Scott went from dead last to first and kept the receipt
stories.dek: Scott leads at 14-6 a year after finishing 12th, looking to add a third championship to his 2010 and 2017 titles.
body: Scott is first at 14-6 after finishing 12th last season. That's a pretty dramatic turnaround for a standings page that spent last year making you scroll all the way down to find him. The league should make him keep his old parking spot anyway. Everybody else needs the exercise less than Scott needs the reminder.

This is the same Scott who entered 2022 as the 12th seed with a 2-12 record and somehow finished ninth. Three places of improvement after a two-win regular season is like rescuing three fries from under the driver's seat. You can call it a recovery. The rest of us would prefer you washed your hands before touching the trophy.

Scott already owns championships from 2010 and 2017, but his most recent trip to the final came in 2023. He went 10-4 and entered as the second seed. Chad got in fifth at 7-7 and finished first. Scott finished second. Chad basically showed up to the airport in flip-flops with a grocery bag and got upgraded while Scott stood there clutching a folder of printed boarding passes. Two championships, and somehow Scott still managed to look like the guy who got bumped from his own flight.

The current Buttkickers have won seven head-to-head games and seven median games. Bryan is a win behind at 13-7, so Scott has earned exactly enough room at the top to set down a drink if he keeps one hand on it. With two championships already on the shelf, Scott can certainly enjoy being in first. Just leave the protective film on the third nameplate, Scott. Even you have to admit the last time you started making room for another trophy, Chad wound up taking the seat.

stories.headline: The Ramblers and Pig Killers must settle who gets the basement
stories.dek: Elam and Todd meet at 7-13, with four weeks left to avoid last place and a one-year suspension.
body: Elam's Ramblers and the Pig Killers have spent ten weeks assembling matching 7-13 records. On the Week 11 schedule, they take their work directly to one another. The winner gets a head-to-head win over the team most immediately in the way of survival. A median win would make it a sweep, and a sweep against an opponent who also misses the median would open a two-win gap. At this end of the table, that qualifies as breathing room.

Elam sits 12th with 1,070.5 season points. Its last three starting totals read 119.7, 127.5 and 113.1. Todd's lineup went 106.8, 104.0 and 176.9 over the same stretch. That last number establishes what the Pig Killers can do. Their 2-8 median record establishes how often the rest of the league has had to worry about it. Todd needs another top-half score while the schedule still offers somebody equally desperate.

After this, Elam gets the 8-12 Cow Tippers, another opponent it can pull closer by beating outright. Todd draws the 14-6 VillageRd Buttkickers. Finding a median win that week would be valuable insurance if the matchup gets away. Elam has managed only three head-to-head wins all season, so having two reachable opponents in a row is an opportunity it can scarcely afford to waste.

The Angry Mennonites are one win above both clubs at 8-12, with a 3-7 median record and consecutive scores of 87.3 and 103.6. They get third-place Smoketown this week, then the Fishsticks. A top-six score against Smoketown would buy Seth some protection while the bottom two play each other. The current cushion is a single win. The standings have issued thicker receipts.

stories.headline: The Fishsticks buy most of Wednesday's waiver bill
stories.dek: Chad spent $125 on Emari Demercado and Pat Bryant, while the team holding the final playoff spot spent zero.
body: The Fishsticks made the most expensive claim on Wednesday's wire and came back for another. Emari Demercado cost $100 with Geno Smith dropped, and Pat Bryant cost $25 with Jordan Addison dropped. That's $125 of the $208 in recorded bids for the day. Chad entered Week 11 at 9-11, one win out of sixth place, and has bought some depth at running back and a different answer at receiver.

Demercado is the more consequential reshuffle because the roster gives up a quarterback slot for a running back. The Fishsticks already have 121.3 points from four C.J. Stroud starts after acquiring him for $8. There's a plausible case for using Smith's spot elsewhere. Demercado's fee, more than twelve times Stroud's, buys the chance to make that case on a starting lineup. The invoice has arrived ahead of the evidence.

VillageRd paid $58 for receiver Elic Ayomanor, with no corresponding drop listed. The move gives the 14-6 league leader another receiver option. Burnin Ballers spent $25 on the Jets defense, while Manny's SexPistols took the Panthers defense for free and dropped Cleveland. Those are two different prices for a new option at the same position, and the eventual starting scores will make a more interesting comparison than the bids alone.

Thatcher's Wackers, the team Chad is chasing, swapped Tutu Atwell for Kalif Raymond on a zero-dollar claim. Atwell himself arrived as a free agent a week earlier. The Wackers have held a weeklong audition at the back of the receiver room for a total charge of zero. Chad needs Bryant or Demercado to give him something he can actually use. The Fishsticks already lead Thatcher in Wednesday's spending, a category ESPN has yet to award a playoff berth for.

stories.headline: Thatcher has points on the receipt while Elam waits to cash in
stories.dek: Drake London and Travis Kelce have started for the Wackers, while both running backs sent to Elam await their first start there.
body: A week after Thatcher's Wackers and Elam's Ramblers traded two players apiece, one side has found room for its acquisitions in the lineup. Drake London has put up 17.9 points in one start for Thatcher, and Travis Kelce has added 5.0 in one. D'Andre Swift and TreVeyon Henderson have yet to start for Elam. The trade has already changed how Thatcher fills two positions. Elam's half of the transaction is still waiting to be called from the bench.

Swift is the interesting piece for a team trying to climb out of 12th. He scored 155.8 points in Thatcher's starting lineup before the deal. Henderson supplied 12.9 there. Those totals describe two very different bodies of work, and Swift gives Elam a running back with a substantial record of usable production in this league. The next question is which existing starter he can improve on. A point scored for Thatcher in October has very little interest in helping Elam in November.

Thatcher can put a figure on what left Elam's lineup, too. London had scored 123.6 for the Ramblers when started, while Kelce had provided 90.2. London has already delivered the larger share of the pair's first 22.9 points for the Wackers. Kelce joins a roster that has already collected 172.5 from Trey McBride across ten starts, so the interesting question is when Thatcher can get useful points from both tight ends.

The timing gives the two clubs different demands. Thatcher has the sixth seed at 10-10 and can use London immediately while sorting out Kelce's place. Elam is 7-13 and has four regular-season weeks to turn a reshaped roster into wins. Swift's first start for the Ramblers, whenever it comes, will tell us more about the deal than another week of admiring his old totals.

stories.headline: McCaffrey scores 50.3, but the supporting cast cannot keep pace
stories.dek: The Fishsticks beat Intercourse Encroachment as both of the top two seeds finish Week 10 without a win.
body: Christian McCaffrey delivered the week's highest listed individual score. Intercourse Encroachment still left Week 10 empty-handed. Bryan's team lost 131.0 to 106.7 against The Fishsticks and finished below the 124.9 median, turning a 50.3-point performance into two losses in the combined standings.

McCaffrey supplied nearly half of Intercourse's total. The rest of the starting lineup combined for 56.4 points, with Michael Penix Jr. the next-highest starter at 12.3. That left little room to absorb the Fishsticks' more evenly shared production: Amon-Ra St. Brown scored 27.3 and C.J. Stroud added 26.4. Chad won despite getting just 1.5 from Rhamondre Stevenson.

The same problem visited the first-place team. Jahmyr Gibbs scored 46.2 for VillageRd Buttkickers and Jared Goff added 29.4, but Scott finished at 118.8. The Bike slashers won with 144.1, led by George Pickens' 44.5 and Mark Andrews' 16.2. VillageRd missed the median as well as the matchup, while Brandon collected both wins.

Those defeats leave Scott first at 14-6 and Bryan second at 13-7. Their positions in the power rankings also survive: Intercourse remains first and VillageRd second. Bryan still leads the league at 142.3 points per game, ahead of Scott's 138.6. One disappointing week has narrowed their room for error without overturning the season's scoring order.

For Chad, the reward reaches beyond beating a higher seed. The Fishsticks are seventh at 9-11 and jump from eighth to fifth in the power rankings, one combined win behind the final playoff position. Brandon is also 9-11, in eighth. The two teams chasing the field did their damage against the league's top two seeds, showing how quickly even a star's best work can disappear into a losing total.

stories.headline: Likely leads Randy's climb as Manny's SexPistols take two wins
stories.dek: A 135.2-point week lifts Randy to fourth in the power rankings, with the playoffs four regular-season weeks away.
body: Randy had 46.4 points sitting on the bench and still found enough in his starting lineup to win twice. Manny's SexPistols beat Elam's Ramblers 135.2 to 113.1 in Week 10, cleared the median and climbed from sixth to fourth in the power rankings. Isaiah Likely led the starters with 30.2 points.

Jayden Daniels supplied another 26.8 at quarterback. Patrick Mahomes' 46.4 stayed on the bench, part of a 103.3-point reserve total that could have made the result feel wasteful. Instead, the chosen lineup delivered the two results that count. Randy sits fourth in the standings at 12-8, level on combined wins with third-place Smoketown Rumspringas.

The contrast with Dwayne's lineup was clear. Ja'Marr Chase scored 34.1 and Cam Skattebo added 27.2 for Elam's Ramblers, but Mike Gesicki contributed only 1.9. Dwayne finished below the 124.9 median and took two losses. His team is now 12th at 7-13 and falls from ninth to 12th in the power rankings.

Randy's result follows a 127.2-point win over Angry Mennonites in Week 9, another week above the median. Across those two finished weeks, Manny's SexPistols have banked four combined wins. Their latest score also improves on their 108.2 in Week 8, when they lost to Cow Tippers and finished below the line. The recent sequence offers a concrete reason for the rise.

The current position comes with a useful cushion: Randy has two more combined wins than sixth-place Thatcher's Wackers, with four weeks left in the 14-week regular season. His next opponent is second-place Intercourse Encroachment, which stands one combined win ahead. The Week 10 recap is a story of points actually converted into progress: a productive tight end, enough quarterback scoring and a lineup that did not need its biggest bench number to move up.

stories.headline: Five double winners tighten the chase below the playoff line
stories.dek: The median rewards five matchup winners, while Smoketown and Burnin Ballers split their two games in very different ways.
body: Week 10 rewarded five teams with the full two wins: The Pig Killers, Cow Tippers, The Bike slashers, Manny's SexPistols and The Fishsticks. Each won its matchup and finished above the 124.9 median. With only six playoff places available, those paired results gave several teams outside the field a useful push toward the line.

Todd set the scoring pace at 176.9 in a 73.2-point victory over Angry Mennonites. Trevor Lawrence contributed 32.8 and Parker Washington added 29.2. The Pig Killers had scored 104.0 the previous week, so this was a 72.9-point improvement. Todd stands 11th at 7-13, three combined wins behind sixth-place Thatcher's Wackers; Seth is 10th at 8-12.

Doug's Cow Tippers joined the double winners by beating Smoketown Rumspringas 152.5 to 138.5. The loss did not leave Roger empty-handed: his total still ranked in the top six and earned a median win. Smoketown remain third at 12-8, while Cow Tippers stand ninth at 8-12. Roger's 152.2-point average across the last three finished weeks is the highest in the power-ranking table.

Burnin Ballers took the opposite route to a split. Burnie's 104.1 beat Thatcher's 85.9 but missed the median, leaving him fifth at 11-9. Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 33.6 and Tony Pollard added 23.9 for the winners. Thatcher received 34.2 from Chuba Hubbard, but the league's lowest team total brought two losses and left the Wackers sixth at 10-10.

That makes the boundary especially narrow. The Fishsticks and Bike slashers are both 9-11, one combined win behind Thatcher, while Cow Tippers and Angry Mennonites sit another win back. Four regular-season weeks remain, with a matchup and a median result available each week. Burnie's split and Roger's split underline the same point from opposite directions: the weekly opponent settles only half of the standings business.

stories.headline: Henry holds the last word in Burnie's chase of Thatcher
stories.dek: Burnin Ballers trail by less than a point, with Derrick Henry still to play against the Chargers on Monday night.
body: Thatcher's Wackers have the lead. Burnin Ballers have Derrick Henry. The narrowest matchup on the Week 10 board heads into Monday night with Thatcher ahead 85.9 to 85.1 so far and Burnie waiting for his last starter to take the field. The next meaningful move belongs to Baltimore's running back.

At the league's 4:11 p.m. Eastern snapshot Monday, Henry had not started. His Ravens face the Chargers at 8:15 p.m. Eastern, and his projection is 19.3 fantasy points. That puts Burnin Ballers' projected total at 104.4, against 85.9 for the Wackers. Thatcher has all nine starters finished; Burnie has eight finished and Henry left.

The standings give that small current gap some weight. Both teams entered the week 10-8, with Thatcher fourth and Burnie sixth. Only six teams make the playoffs, and the regular season runs 14 weeks. This is a direct meeting between teams sitting inside the field, with the last qualifying seed on one side of the scoreboard.

There is a second contest to watch, though Henry's projected workload on the fantasy scoreboard does not put Burnie above the median. Burnin Ballers sit 35.8 points below the current median of 120.9. Their projected total remains 22.4 below the projected median of 126.8. A head-to-head comeback and a median win are separate assignments.

Thatcher, meanwhile, is 35.0 below the current median and has no starters left to add points. The Wackers' immediate hope is that their slim matchup lead survives. Burnie's is that Henry supplies enough to pass it, then keeps going. Neither the matchup nor the week's median result is being treated as final; Monday's remaining game still has its say.

stories.headline: Scott chases a moving line while Chad waits at 131.0
stories.dek: VillageRd Buttkickers are below both median measures, with Ravens D/ST left and The Fishsticks just above the projected line.
body: The league leader has work left on two scoreboards. VillageRd Buttkickers sit at 114.8 points so far, below the current median and behind The Bike slashers in their matchup. Scott still has Ravens D/ST against the Chargers on Monday night, but the projection leaves him short of both targets.

The current median is 120.9, putting VillageRd 6.1 points below it. The projected median rises to 126.8, while Scott's projected total is 122.6, a gap of 4.2. Baltimore's defense is projected for 7.8 points in the 8:15 p.m. Eastern game. The distinction matters: gaining on today's line is not the same as clearing where the line is projected to finish.

Chad's Fishsticks occupy the other side of that squeeze. Their nine starters have finished with 131.0 points, leaving them 10.1 above the current median but only 4.2 above the projected one. They have no remaining starter to answer any late movement. Their head-to-head score so far is also favorable, ahead of Intercourse Encroachment's 106.7.

Brandon has more than a spectator's role. The Bike slashers lead VillageRd with 127.9 points and still have Mark Andrews in the same Baltimore game. Their projected total is 134.8, which sits 8.0 above the projected median. Scott must chase a matchup opponent who can still add points, as well as a league threshold that can move.

That makes Monday's defensive points especially relevant to a team that entered Week 10 first at 14-4. The Fishsticks and Bike slashers both entered 7-11, looking up at the six-team playoff field. The top six weekly scores earn median wins regardless of opponent. For now Chad and Brandon are above both measures, while Scott is below both; those are live positions, not settled results.

stories.headline: Flowers gets the chase as Cow Tippers sit on 152.5
stories.dek: Smoketown have one starter left to cut Doug's lead, while Todd's 176.9 sets the scoring pace so far.
body: Cow Tippers have put up their number. Smoketown Rumspringas still have Zay Flowers. Doug leads their Week 10 matchup 152.5 to 127.1 so far, leaving Roger's last starter to pursue a total that will receive no more points from Cow Tippers' lineup. Flowers faces the Chargers with Baltimore at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Monday.

The projection favors Doug's current position. Flowers is projected for 14.9 points, taking Smoketown to a projected 141.9. Cow Tippers have all nine starters finished; Roger has eight finished. A performance above the receiver's projection would be needed to threaten the lead. Nothing has been recorded as a final matchup result in the live snapshot.

Both quarterbacks have already supplied plenty. Brock Purdy scored 43.7 fantasy points for Cow Tippers, while Joe Burrow contributed 41.2 for Smoketown. Doug also received 37.1 from running back Emmett Johnson. Those are already-played contributions, giving Flowers a clear target rather than a duel with an opposing starter still on the field.

The median picture offers Roger a separate route to a useful week. Smoketown stand 6.2 above the current median of 120.9, and their projected total is 15.1 above the projected median of 126.8. Cow Tippers are 31.6 above the current line and 25.7 above the projected one. Even as the head-to-head chase continues, both teams occupy the upper half of the live scoring table.

Above them all so far are Todd's Pig Killers at 176.9, with all nine starters finished and a lead over Angry Mennonites' 103.6. Todd entered last at 5-13; Doug entered 11th at 6-12, while Roger stood third at 11-7. Two teams near the bottom have supplied the highest totals so far. Monday now asks whether Flowers can change one of their matchup leads before Week 10 closes.
